Representation of Blobby Object
❖ Blobby objects : changes its shape over time (during motion) i.e., it does not 
maintain a fixed shape.
❖ Examples : Water droplets, human muscles, melting objects, molecular 
structures, and so on.
❖ The shapes of blobby objects exhibit certain degree of fluidity.
❖ Characteristics like fluidity can not be adequately depicted by simply with 
spherical or elliptical shapes. 
❖ Several methods have been developed to represent blobby objects. One way 
to do this is to combine the Gaussian density function.
(a) Water droplets
(b) Human muscles

Spline Representation
❖ Widely used approach to represent 3D objects in Computer Graphics. 
                                                     Why?
❖Core problem : To represent a curve/surface of any shape.   
Boundary Representation Techniques
2

❖Core problem : To represent a curve/surface of any shape.   
❖Line segment-based approximation: 
❖Line segment should be very-very small so that the represented curve looks 
smoother. 
❖ For that, we have to provide sufficiently large no. of points, which we do 
not want.
❖ Curve-based approximation:
❖ We do not have equations for all set of possible curves. 
❖What is desirable?
❖ User can only provide a small no. of (either on curve itself or its nearby points 
called control points) control points, and the system let it interpolate these control 
points to generate the desired curve.
